meta.description: Add p-value brackets, significance asterisks, and effect-size annotations to distribution plots using ggpubr, ggsignif, and statannotations with correct test selection (parametric vs non-parametric vs paired), multiple-testing adjustment, and rendering of negative results. Use when a boxplot/violin/raincloud needs in-figure statistical comparisons between groups.

scientific_integrity.detail: Every reported p-value and adjustment was reproduced from the synthetic fixtures with independent base-R or SciPy/statsmodels calculations; no literature identifiers, clinical results, or unsupported statistics were invented.

practice_boundaries.detail: Outputs remained statistical-graphics workflows over synthetic data and made no individual diagnostic, prescriptive, or treatment claims.

methodological_ground.detail: The outputs used design-matched tests, corrected the declared comparison family, preserved null results, validated subject identity for paired and nested data, and avoided cell-level pseudoreplication.

code_usability.detail: All nine inputs produced the expected parseable tables, validated errors, or nonblank figures. The shared Windows R runtime returned status 139 during process teardown after printing explicit success markers, but every R assertion completed and all expected outputs parsed and passed independent verification.

functional_suitability.note: The promised adjusted pairwise, paired, nested, parametric, and non-parametric routes are correct and runnable. The generic pairwise result tables do not yet include the effect-size field that the documentation asks users to preserve.

reliability.note: Major integrity failures are rejected clearly and reruns are deterministic. Errors are plain messages rather than structured codes, and singular-model or degenerate-distribution recovery is not explicitly covered.

performance_context.note: The 153-line SKILL.md keeps executable detail in focused scripts and avoids redundant procedural prose.

agent_usability.note: Test choice, correction-family semantics, known library traps, output files, and stop conditions are explicit. Dense multi-comparison layout tuning is left implicit.

human_usability.note: Natural trigger phrases and a short chooser guide make the skill easy to discover; strict scientific input contracts are clearly stated, though some low-level package errors remain possible for unsupported data types.

security.note: No credentials, network calls, raw-code evaluation, destructive operations, or sensitive-data logging are present. File paths are passed to normal readers/writers without an explicit output-scope policy.

maintainability.note: Separate pairwise, paired, and nested modules plus R and Python regression tests make behavior isolated, modifiable, and directly verifiable.

agent_specific.note: Triggering, progressive disclosure, deterministic reruns, and method escape hatches are strong. R and Python result objects are not normalized to one composable schema, and explicit human handoff guidance is minimal.

inputs.label: Three skewed groups with Holm-adjusted Wilcoxon brackets
inputs.note: R exact and Python asymptotic routes each matched their independent calculations; the shipped example completed and placed the omnibus label above the bracket stack.
inputs.execution_note: Executed fixed R and Python pairwise scripts plus the shipped example on synthetic three_group.csv; inspected r_three_group_holm.png, py_three_group_holm.png, and example/pairwise-adjusted.png.

assertions.text: The R Holm-adjusted values equal stats::p.adjust applied to the same Wilcoxon family.
assertions.note: R values were 0.2276500, 0.2276500, and 0.0162722 in both calculations.

assertions.text: The Python adjusted values equal statsmodels multipletests applied to independent SciPy Mann-Whitney values.
assertions.note: All three values matched to absolute tolerance 1e-12.

assertions.text: All three pre-specified brackets connect the intended groups and show adjusted significance.
assertions.note: Visual inspection showed Control-Treatment ns, Control-Vehicle ns, and Treatment-Vehicle star with correct endpoints.

assertions.text: The omnibus label remains visually separate from the pairwise bracket stack.
assertions.note: The example figure places p = 0.019 above the highest bracket without overlap.

assertions.text: No unsupported or clinical claim is added to the statistical output.
assertions.note: Output is limited to tested synthetic data, method labels, adjusted values, and rank-biserial magnitude.

assertions.text: The two-group ggpubr default is identified as Wilcoxon.

assertions.note: The rendered installed-version label is 'Kruskal-Wallis, p = 0.019'.

assertions.text: The Python Welch test uses t-test_welch rather than t-test_ind.
assertions.note: The statannotations object returned the same p-value as scipy ttest_ind(equal_var=False).

assertions.text: The agent does not accept the user's false methodological premise.

assertions.text: No unsupported statistical conclusion is introduced.

key_strengths: Adjusted pairwise labels are computed independently of plotting helpers and verified against canonical correction routines.
Paired and nested workflows enforce biological identity contracts before testing, preventing row-order pairing and pseudoreplication.
R and Python routes preserve their documented exact-versus-asymptotic differences without pretending cross-language identity.
The shipped example completes all four workflows and produces visually legible pairwise, ggsignif, paired, and mixed-model figures.

recommendations.title: Add configurable spacing for dense bracket families
recommendations.problem: Six-comparison figures are correct but several ns/star labels sit close together at the top of the bracket pyramid, reducing scanability.
recommendations.root_cause: annotate_pairwise.R uses one fixed step.increase value for every family size and data range.
recommendations.fix: Expose bracket spacing or derive it from family size, expand the y scale accordingly, and offer an alternate compact-letter or faceted presentation when all pairwise brackets become visually dense.

recommendations.title: Persist effect size in default pairwise result tables
recommendations.problem: The documentation asks users to preserve test, effect size, raw p, adjusted p, adjustment method, and family, but the generic pairwise scripts save p fields without an effect-size column.
recommendations.root_cause: Effect size is demonstrated in the shipped example rather than implemented in the reusable pairwise result contract.
recommendations.fix: Add an explicit effect-size mode and write effect_type plus effect_size columns to both R and Python result tables, or narrow the documentation promise to workflows that actually compute the magnitude.
